title: apply's alias check for a rules finding's word pair reads every alias file but kb/_self's own, so a pair whose term kb/_self/_retrieval/aliases.csv holds gets a second row
goal: Found by the fresh-context review of SP-sz5fbvqn, item ST-rhnku4mc (apply writes a kb/_self aliases row for a rules finding that names a word pair): the check that a rules finding's pair is in no alias file yet (ql_apply.rules_alias_rows through Gate.alias_terms) reads kb/_self/_retrieval/aliases.csv too (kbfacts.alias_files(rules=True) or the same set), so a pair whose term or canonical that file already holds writes no second row and the finding is left as the goal says.

run: import sys,csv; sys.path.insert(0,'_tools'); import ql_apply,kbfacts; t=ql_apply.Gate().alias_terms(); rows=list(csv.DictReader(open(kbfacts.SELF_ALIASES,encoding='utf-8'))); miss=[r['term'] for r in rows if ' '.join(r['term'].lower().split()) not in t]; print(miss[:5]); sys.exit(1 if miss else 0)

gates.question: Should Gate.alias_terms read kb/_self/_retrieval/aliases.csv by default, with an article's alias candidates (alias_fixes) opting out, or the other way round?
options: default-rules: alias_terms(rules=True) by default; alias_fixes passes rules=False
opt-in: alias_terms() as before; rules_alias_rows passes rules=True
gates.recommendation: default-rules: alias_terms(rules=True) by default; alias_fixes passes rules=False
gates.answer: default-rules: alias_terms(rules=True) by default; alias_fixes passes rules=False
